language: mixed

ORDER BY st.order, f.id

RETURN r.id, r.text, d.name, o1.name, a.name, o2.name
ORDER BY r.id

Write the service id as $sid and variant ids as $variant_ids; never write ids or names as literals.
Use $variant_ids only when variants are given and the graph can filter on them.
Use only the labels, relationship types and properties in the schema.
End with LIMIT.
Schema:
Service {id}
Step {id, order, citizen_action}
Fee {id, label, amount_min, amount_max, unit, note, condition_text}
Variant {id, dimension}
(Service)-[:HAS_STEP]->(Step)
(Service)-[:HAS_FEE]->(Fee)
(Step)-[:CHARGES]->(Fee)
(Fee)-[:APPLIES_WHEN]->(Variant)

service: birth_registration_timely
intent: fees
variants: birth_status=non_marital
language: en
request: "parents who are not married: Is there a fee for birth certificate registration, and how much?"

Translate the citizen request into ONE read-only Cypher query for the charter graph.
Output only the query.
Write the service id as $sid and variant ids as $variant_ids; never write ids or names as literals.
Use $variant_ids only when variants are given and the graph can filter on them.
Use only the labels, relationship types and properties in the schema.
End with LIMIT.
Schema:
Service {id}
Requirement {id, text, group, parent_id, min_required, condition_text}
Variant {id, dimension}
(Service)-[:REQUIRES]->(Requirement)
(Requirement)-[:APPLIES_WHEN]->(Variant)

service: cho_dental_services
intent: requirements
variants: none
language: en
request: "I want to apply for toothache. What should I prepare?"

MATCH (s:Service {id: $sid})-[:REQUIRES]->(r:Requirement)
RETURN r.id, r.text, r.group, r.parent_id, r.min_required, r.condition_text
ORDER BY r.id
LIMIT 50
